title: Kit snapshot, version 1
description: What one Mac's Kit sends up on /mac as the payload of a snapshot message: the rows of the four groups the phone shows, the idle sessions with a message kept in the Kit in the last 24 hours, the usage, and the version of the archived list. Times are Unix seconds. Labels are cut to 160 characters on the Mac. No field holds a prompt, a reply, a transcript line, a file's contents or a path; a kept message's subject and text go up, never its link or an address. See phone/DESIGN.md, section 3.

v.description: Format version. A new required field or a changed meaning makes a new version.

at.description: When the Mac built this snapshot.

name.description: The Mac's name, as in System Settings > General > Sharing.

tz.description: IANA time zone of the Mac.

account.description: A short hash of the Claude Code login, to merge usage across Macs. Never the address.

paused.description: Auto effort is off for every session.

credits_all.description: Use credits at the usage limit, from the Kit's Settings.

alerts_off.description: Sent, as true, only while Alerts are off in Reach me by on this Mac: nothing alerts outside the Kit (no email, Chat, text, Mac notice or Needs you push), and each message is kept in the Kit (rows[].messages). Absent: alerts are on, as from a Kit before this field.

reach.description: The names of the Reach me by ways only. Never an address, number or webhook.

at.description: When the Kit read the usage. Null when it never read it.

kind.description: The usage API's kind: session (the 5-hour limit), weekly_all, or a weekly limit of one model.

name.description: As the window shows it: 5-hour limit, Weekly, Weekly, Opus.

reached.description: Set while a limit is reached: sessions hold until it resets.

archived_rev.description: The version of this Mac's archived list (a hash of its items as the phone sees them). The list itself goes up only when the server asks with want_archived. Null when the Mac has no list yet.

level.description: Effort. The phone shows xhigh as Extra.

url.description: The claude.ai link that Open in Claude uses.

id.description: The row id the window uses.

sid.description: The Claude Code session id, when the Mac knows it.

group.description: Needs you, Claude working, Waiting on someone else, Held at usage limit; idle: a session the Claude app lists that needs nothing now but has a message kept in the Kit in the last 24 hours (other idle sessions never go up). An idle row's sub is Message: and the subject, its time_at when the newest kept message came.

sub.description: The row's second line, as the window draws it.

sub_strong.description: A part of the second line drawn in bold, such as an effort level.

sub_warn.description: A part of the second line drawn as a warning, such as 1 check failing.

late.description: The time column is drawn as a warning (it waited on the person 10 minutes or more).

time_at.description: What the time column counts from (needs you, working) or to (a wait's deadline, a hold's end).

manual.description: The person set the effort (Auto is off for this session).

reason.description: Why the Kit chose the level.

why.description: Why it needs the person, in one short line.

turn_at.description: When the turn now running started.

background.description: What still runs after the turn.

checkin.description: Optional. The latest progress check-in of the work that runs now (Claude working only): the Kit's short note on what got done and what is next, written by Haiku every 15 minutes while the work runs. Null when there is none, and when the work ends. A Kit from before it sends no checkin.

note.description: 2 or 3 short sentences. Cut to 400 characters on the Mac.

hold.description: Held at the usage limit, or at the session's own percentage.
True for a session set to Never use credits (it holds at its own percentage); false for a wait at the usage limit.

percent.description: The limit's percentage when it held.

limit.description: The name of the limit it holds for: 5-hour limit, Weekly.

until.description: When it goes on: the limit's reset.

limit_mode.description: The session's At the usage limit setting.

mode.description: follow: same as Settings. credits: always use credits. hold: never use credits; hold at the percentage.

messages.description: Optional, on a row of any group: the messages this session or the Kit would have sent to the person by email, Chat, a text or a notice, kept in the Kit instead, in the last 24 hours, newest first. Sent only when there is one.

alerts.description: The session's alerts. true: the person turned them on for this session, so it reaches them the Reach me by ways. false: off, as every session starts and stays until the person turns them on, so nothing about it goes out and its messages stay in the Kit app on the Mac. Optional: a Kit from before the switch sends none, and the phone reads that as true, since such a Kit has no switch.

message.description: A message kept in the Kit, not sent. No link and no address ever goes up.

at.description: When it would have been sent.

subject.description: Its subject, as it would have been sent.

text.description: Its words, with their line breaks; cut to 1000 characters on the Mac. Never its link.

why.description: The Mac's words for why it was not sent: alerts are off, alerts are off for this session.

replied.description: Optional: when the person replied, themselves, where this message is about (the same email thread, Chat space or Asana task). The message is handled; the page says You replied and the time. Never where, or what they wrote. A Kit from before it sends none.

what.description: What it waits for. For a check-prompt with no --what: A yes/no check. Never the wait's target (thread id, pull request), script or question.

from.description: For an email reply: the sender's domain or name the session gave.

why.description: The deadline's reason, as the session gave it.

checks.description: How the Kit checks it, in words: Your email, every 30 min, 7 AM to 9 PM.

replied.description: Optional, on an email reply: when the person replied in its thread themselves. Their own reply does not end the wait; it still waits for the other person. Never the thread, or what they wrote. A Kit from before it sends none.
